2.3 Skin tone, imaging type and fairness
Transfer learning from ImageNet is the common starting point, and both CNNs and transformers are used.
Class imbalance is handled by resampling, class weights or focal loss; accuracy alone hides poor results on rare classes.
Explanation maps such as Grad-CAM are often shown, but rarely tested for whether they point at what the model uses.
Several works add a segmentation or cropping step, or split the task into stages.
Ensembles report the highest numbers but cost more to run.
2.7 Limitations of the literature and how this work responds
Most studies use one training run. Here: the supporting studies use three seeds.
Skin tone and non-tumour conditions are rarely tested. Here: the models are tested on Indian clinical images, including thousands of non-tumour conditions.
Explanations are seldom evaluated. Here: Grad-CAM maps are scored against random maps.
Selection on test data is not always ruled out. Here: every choice is made on validation data, and automatic sanity checks confirm it.
